questions.q: The compound that reacts with nitrous acid to give yellow oily liquid is __________.
questions.solution:
A **secondary** amine gives an N-nitrosoamine, a yellow oily liquid:

$\mathrm{C_6H_5NHCH_3} + \mathrm{HNO_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5N(NO)CH_3} + \mathrm{H_2O}$

Aniline, a primary amine, forms a diazonium salt; N,N-dimethylaniline is nitrosated on the ring; nitrobenzene does not react.

questions.q: Aniline is a weaker base than methylamine because:
options: aniline has a higher molar mass
the lone pair on nitrogen is delocalised into the benzene ring
questions.solution:
In aniline the nitrogen lone pair is **drawn into the ring by resonance**, so it is less available to accept a proton.

In methylamine the methyl group pushes electron density onto nitrogen, making the lone pair more available.

questions.q: The carbylamine reaction (chloroform and alcoholic KOH) is given by:
questions.solution:
Only **primary** amines give an isocyanide, recognised by its **offensive smell**.

$\mathrm{RNH_2} + \mathrm{CHCl_3} + 3\mathrm{KOH} \rightarrow \mathrm{RNC} + 3\mathrm{KCl} + 3\mathrm{H_2O}$

questions.q: In the Hinsberg test, the sulphonamide formed from a primary amine:
questions.solution:
Benzenesulphonyl chloride converts a **primary** amine to $\mathrm{C_6H_5SO_2NHR}$. The N–H left is acidic, so the sulphonamide **dissolves in alkali**.

A secondary amine gives $\mathrm{C_6H_5SO_2NR_2}$ with no acidic H, insoluble in alkali. A tertiary amine does not react.

questions.q: When aniline reacts with acetic anhydride, the product formed is :
questions.solution:
The acetyl group goes onto the **nitrogen**, not the ring:

$\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2} + \mathrm{(CH_3CO)_2O} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5NHCOCH_3} + \mathrm{CH_3COOH}$

The product is **acetanilide**. Acetylation is also how the $\mathrm{{-}NH_2}$ group is protected before nitration.

questions.q: Benzenediazonium chloride is prepared from aniline by treatment with:
questions.solution:
Diazotisation uses nitrous acid, made in situ from $\mathrm{NaNO_2}$ and HCl, kept **ice cold** at $0$–$5\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

Above that temperature the diazonium salt decomposes, releasing nitrogen and forming phenol.

questions.q: Benzenediazonium chloride warmed with CuCl and HCl gives chlorobenzene. This is called:
questions.solution:
With cuprous salts, CuCl/HCl or CuBr/HBr or CuCN/KCN, it is the **Sandmeyer reaction**.

The Gattermann reaction does the same job with copper powder and the halogen acid.

questions.q: Benzenediazonium chloride couples with phenol in mildly alkaline solution to give:
questions.solution:
The diazonium ion attacks the **para** position of phenol, giving **p-hydroxyazobenzene**, an orange dye.

The $\mathrm{{-}N{=}N{-}}$ group linking two rings forms an extended conjugated system, which is why azo compounds are coloured.

questions.q: Nitrobenzene is reduced by Sn and HCl to:
questions.solution:
In **acid** with a metal, the nitro group is reduced completely: $\mathrm{C_6H_5NO_2} + 6[\mathrm{H}] \rightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2} + 2\mathrm{H_2O}$, giving **aniline**.

In neutral or alkaline conditions the reduction stops at intermediate products such as phenylhydroxylamine or azobenzene.

questions.q: How many amines, primary, secondary and tertiary together, have the formula $\mathrm{C_3H_9N}$?
questions.solution:
Primary: propan-1-amine and propan-2-amine.

Secondary: N-methylethanamine.

Tertiary: N,N-dimethylmethanamine.

Total **4**.

questions.q: How many carbon atoms are in the amine formed when butanamide undergoes Hoffmann bromamide degradation?
questions.solution: Butanamide has 4 carbons. One leaves as carbonate, so the product, propan-1-amine, has **3**.

questions.q: What mass of aniline, in grams, is obtained from $12.3\,\mathrm{g}$ of nitrobenzene if the reduction is complete? ($\mathrm{C_6H_5NO_2} = 123$, $\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2} = 93$.)
questions.solution:
One mole of nitrobenzene gives one mole of aniline.

Moles $= \dfrac{12.3}{123} = 0.1$, so mass of aniline $= 0.1 \times 93 = \mathbf{9.3\,g}$.

questions.q: How many moles of $\mathrm{N_2}$ are released when $0.25\,\mathrm{mol}$ of benzenediazonium chloride is warmed with water?
questions.solution: $\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2Cl} + \mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5OH} + \mathrm{N_2} + \mathrm{HCl}$: one mole of $\mathrm{N_2}$ per mole of salt, so **0.25 mol**.

questions.q: The $\mathrm{p}K_b$ of methylamine is $3.38$ and that of aniline is $9.38$. By what power of ten is methylamine the stronger base? (Give the exponent.)
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{K_b(\mathrm{CH_3NH_2})}{K_b(\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2})} = 10^{9.38 - 3.38} = 10^{6}$.

The exponent is **6**: methylamine is a million times the stronger base, which shows how much resonance with the ring costs aniline's lone pair.

questions.q: Starting from benzene, show how you would prepare (a) aniline, (b) phenol via a diazonium salt, (c) chlorobenzene via a diazonium salt, and (d) p-hydroxyazobenzene. Give the conditions for each step.
questions.solution:
**(a) Benzene to aniline.** Nitrate with conc. $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ and conc. $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ below $330\,\mathrm{K}$ to get nitrobenzene. Reduce with Sn and HCl, then free the base with NaOH.

$\mathrm{C_6H_6} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5NO_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2}$

**Diazotisation** (common to b–d). Aniline with $\mathrm{NaNO_2}$ and HCl at $273$–$278\,\mathrm{K}$ gives benzenediazonium chloride, $\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^-}$. It must be used cold and at once.

**(b) Phenol.** Warm the diazonium solution with water: $\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2Cl} + \mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5OH} + \mathrm{N_2} + \mathrm{HCl}$.

**(c) Chlorobenzene.** Sandmeyer reaction with CuCl and HCl: $\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2Cl} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5Cl} + \mathrm{N_2}$.

**(d) p-Hydroxyazobenzene.** Couple the cold diazonium salt with phenol (made as in b) in mildly alkaline solution. Attack is at the para position: $\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2Cl} + \mathrm{C_6H_5OH} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5N{=}NC_6H_4OH} + \mathrm{HCl}$, an orange dye.
